evaluations.evidence: create a new game
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes complementary capabilities for games (invite/join, run rounds, browse/view/export/delete), so game creation is not a missing prerequisite.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL
evaluations.rationale: Complementary capability exists for estimators to use the URL and join the game.

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes complementary capabilities to view/select items and for participants to see the current item and estimate it.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Items are created/added via other stories, so listing them is supported by complementary creation behavior.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes ways to create/add items and to re-estimate earlier items, so selection/re-selection is not missing prerequisites.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items
evaluations.rationale: Complementary capabilities exist to view/select/edit/delete items, forming a complete item lifecycle.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes creation/addition of items, so editing existing items does not expose a missing creation capability.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes creation/addition of items, so deletion does not expose a missing prerequisite.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Backlog lacks an explicit story for participants/estimators to submit/play an estimate (choose a card). Showing estimates presupposes estimate capture.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Accepting an average presupposes that estimates are captured; backlog has reveal/change behaviors but no explicit estimate submission story.

evaluations.evidence: if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Auto-filling based on played cards presupposes a capability for estimators to play/select a card; no explicit story covers submitting an estimate.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Entering a final estimate can be done by the moderator independent of how individual estimates are captured; complementary transcript/export stories exist to use stored results.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes selecting items for (re-)estimation and viewing prior rounds, supporting re-estimation flow.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Imported stories complement existing item listing/selection/edit/delete capabilities; no missing prerequisite is implied.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/paste is an alternative creation path for items and is complemented by item management stories.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes game creation and transcript viewing/exporting, so browsing previous games has complementary stored-game capabilities.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes creating/running games and exporting transcripts; transcript viewing is supported by complementary game lifecycle stories.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Transcript export is complemented by transcript viewing and game storage/lifecycle stories.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Transcript export is complemented by transcript viewing and game storage/lifecycle stories.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes game creation and browsing/viewing previous games, so deletion has complementary create/read capabilities.

evaluations.evidence: create an account
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes login, change details, delete account, and password reminder, forming a complete account lifecycle.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Account creation exists, so login does not expose a missing prerequisite.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Account creation exists, so updating details has the necessary complementary capability.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Account creation exists, so deletion has complementary create capability; game deletion also exists for stored data management.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: This is a cross-cutting display capability and does not imply a missing complementary CRUD step in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminder complements login/account usage; account creation exists.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {…} or {…}
evaluations.rationale: This is a configuration option; it does not expose a missing prerequisite capability beyond the general estimating flow.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Invitation is complemented by estimator join behavior; the limit does not imply missing complementary steps.

evaluations.evidence: join a game ... received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes moderator invitation via URL and game creation, so joining has complementary prerequisites.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes creating/adding items and selecting an item to estimate, so displaying the current item is supported.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Items are created/added/imported elsewhere, so participant listing does not expose a missing creation capability.

evaluations.evidence: see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Requires the system to record that an estimator submitted an estimate; backlog lacks an explicit story for submitting/playing an estimate.

evaluations.evidence: after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Depends on a capability for estimators to give/submit an estimate; backlog has reveal/change/visibility but no explicit estimate submission story.

evaluations.evidence: be able to change my estimate
evaluations.rationale: Changing an estimate presupposes an initial estimate submission capability, which is not explicitly present in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Requires storing per-estimator estimates over time; backlog lacks an explicit story for capturing/submitting estimates in the first place.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Seeing who gave what requires that estimates are captured and associated with estimators; no explicit estimate submission story exists.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer
evaluations.rationale: Timer functionality is self-contained and does not imply missing complementary CRUD capabilities elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Depends on the capability for participants to play/submit an estimate; backlog lacks an explicit estimate submission story.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes transcript viewing/exporting and item listing, supporting access to prior-round information at a feature level.

evaluations.evidence: cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: This is a UI consistency requirement and does not expose a missing complementary capability in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Changing an estimate presupposes an initial estimate submission capability, which is not explicitly present in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Displaying a participant photo presupposes a way to provide/upload/set that photo; no story covers capturing or managing participant photos.

evaluations.evidence: compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Non-functional compliance does not imply missing complementary functional steps in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Glossary/documentation story is self-contained and does not require complementary CRUD capabilities to be feature-complete.

evaluations.evidence: created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Implementation detail/performance story does not expose a missing complementary functional capability.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Cross-browser support is non-functional and does not imply missing complementary functional steps.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility compliance is non-functional and does not expose missing complementary functional capabilities.

evaluations.evidence: respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Performance requirement does not imply missing complementary CRUD/functional steps for feature completeness.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Internationalization support is non-functional/technical and does not expose missing complementary functional steps.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: URL design is non-functional/architectural and does not imply missing complementary functional capabilities.

evaluations.evidence: nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Error page handling is cross-cutting and does not expose a missing complementary functional step in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Requires capturing and storing 'results' (estimates) for later study; backlog lacks an explicit story for submitting/capturing individual estimates, which is prerequisite to storing them (identifiable or not).

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Metrics require collecting/recording usage events/data; backlog has no complementary story establishing analytics/usage data capture needed to compute metrics.
